title: Illegal Nvidia Blackwell B300 GPUs Found in China Telecom's Network
summary:
A government-linked telecommunications provider in China utilized restricted AI hardware that was prohibited by export regulations. The infrastructure of state-owned China Telecom was identified as containing illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs.

Nvidia has asserted that recent court cases show less than 0.5% of its export-controlled chips were diverted to China. Critics maintain that this figure only accounts for criminal indictments pursued by the DOJ and FBI when convictions are highly likely, suggesting that total smuggling remains a larger problem.

selectedTweets.text:
Nvidia's statement in this article--asserting that recent court cases found that "less than one half of one percent" of export controlled chips were diverted to China--is just beyond absurd. Perhaps what Nvidia means is that the DOJ has only brought cases (which DOJ only pursues when it is confident it will win a conviction, for which it must clear a high evidentiary bar) against people for diverting 0.5% of its controlled chips to China. 

But if the DOJ has brought criminal indictments against people for smuggling one out of every two hundred products you ship, to me that seems like a lot! And obviously basic logic tells you that the number of actual smuggling incidents is far, far higher than those disclosed in indictments. Ants, kitchen, etc. 

Chip smuggling is a real problem. It's great that the DOJ and FBI are actively trying to combat it. But claims like this are just straight-up misinformation, and Nvidia's years-long denial of the significance of the smuggling problem, despite massive evidence to the contrary, is simply pathological. This all just calls into question whether Nvidia is doing any more than the bare minimum legally required to combat the threat.
